items.name: v0.40.14
items.body:
## What's Changed
* `ollama launch claude` now applies the model's output token limit for Claude Code, so cloud models no longer run into the 128k default cap
* Cloud web search responses on `/api/chat` are now decoded correctly, including compressed responses
* OpenAI-compatible endpoints no longer override a model's packaged sampler defaults — clients that send no `temperature`/`top_p` get the model's own values instead of 1.0, matching `/api/chat`
* `/v1/responses` now preserves readable input content, including prior assistant refusals, instead of flattening it
* Ollama's app can now retry ChatGPT disconnect failures instead of leaving the connection in a broken state
* `ollama launch codex` verifies ChatGPT routing before configuring, and reports a clear error when routing is unavailable
* Faster top-k sampling on MLX for large vocabularies

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.13...v0.40.14

items.name: ai@7.0.162
items.body:
### Patch Changes

- 857ca45: Restore server-defined tool metadata, dynamic status, and title when validating tool approval continuations so approval policies receive the same tool definition fields as new model calls.
- 4d6d830: Support a single telemetry operation for durable `WorkflowAgent` runs, including the prompt, final output, steps, and tools. Events recorded in the workflow are reported on completion or suspension with their original timestamps. For OpenTelemetry, pass the same `OpenTelemetryIdGenerator` instance as the tracer provider's `idGenerator` and `sampler` and as `new OpenTelemetry({ durable })`. This explicit bridge carries parent trace context and sampling across steps, reports model spans live with provider requests nested beneath them, and reconstructs the enclosing `invoke_agent` tree when the run completes. Without the bridge, existing live per-model tracing is preserved. Add typed experimental durable context hooks for telemetry integrations; remove reliance on process-global ID-generator detection.
- Updated dependencies [fa15312]
  - @ai-sdk/provider-utils@5.0.74
  - @ai-sdk/gateway@4.0.135

items.name: v0.40.12
items.body:
## Liquid AI LFM3

[LFM3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3) is Liquid AI's new family of small models built for local agents, tool calling, and structured output, on Liquid's new tri-hybrid architecture. The family includes:

- [lfm3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3): a 1.7B text model with a 256K-token context window
- [lfm3-vl](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-vl): adds image understanding
- [lfm3-audio](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-audio): speech recognition, translation, and text-to-speech in 18 languages
- [lfm3-omni](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-omni): text, images, and audio in one model

```sh
ollama run lfm3
```

## d1 decision models

Liquid AI's d1 models now come in a 2B size, built on LFM3. [d1](https://ollama.com/library/d1) makes decisions about text and images, and [d1-omni](https://ollama.com/library/d1-omni) adds audio.

```sh
ollama run d1:2b "I was charged twice for order 4417." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

Note: lfm3 and d1 2b are supported on Apple hardware in this release.  Support for Linux/Windows coming soon.

## What's Changed
- Faster prompt processing on Apple silicon for Gemma 4, Flint and Laguna models
- Speculative decoding now supports DFlash2 draft models on MLX
- Gemma 4 keeps more detail in small images
- `ollama launch` now works with OpenCode v2
- Fixed tool-only assistant turns from Kimi CLI
- Updated MLX and llama.cpp

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.11...v0.40.12

items.name: v0.40.11
items.body:
## Speech

Ollama can now generate [speech](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech) on macOS. `ollama run` plays text or a chat model's reply aloud as the audio is generated, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint.

```sh
ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama."
```

## d3 decision models

[d3](https://ollama.com/library/d3) brings vLLM Semantic Router's decision models to Ollama. Give a model text, structured state, or an image, and ask it to classify, answer yes or no, or score options with probabilities. The family includes 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B sizes.

```sh
ollama run d3 "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

## New Contributors
* @SynapShift made their first contribution in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19173

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.10...v0.40.11

items.name: v2.3.0
items.body:
### Features

* **api:** add Claude Tag endpoints for Claude Enterprise organizations


### Bug Fixes

* **google-cloud:** send user profiles requests to the organization endpoint


### Chores

* **client:** stop sending query params hardcoded in endpoint paths
* **docs:** improve the descriptions of the code execution tool and its encrypted results
* **docs:** reword work queue, skill and external key descriptions
* **docs:** update descriptions of the per-user usage and cost reports
* **internal:** carry endpoint path query params to the request layer
* **internal:** check the repository by owner and public name in workflows
* **internal:** read the beta route qualifier instead of the beta=true query
* **internal:** remove preview build upload from CI
* **internal:** stop sending the beta query param from parse and stream


### Documentation

* **mcp:** remove the stray `await` from the async `tool_runner` examples
* **google-cloud:** update the product name
* **client:** link the Bedrock and Vertex raw response docstrings to the SDK documentation
* update the README and the example request

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| `@modelcontextprotocol/client` | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server` | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/core` | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy` | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/codemod` | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/node` | 2.1.2 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/express`, `hono`, `fastify` | unchanged |

## Upgrade notes

- **`x-mcp-header` on a `number` parameter is rejected**, as the 2026-07-28 spec requires: the client does not list such a tool, and the server answers a call to it with `-32020`. Use `z.int()` or remove the annotation. (#2762, #2960)
- **`outputSchema` from `z.object(...).meta({ id })`.** On a 2025-11-25 connection the result is no longer wrapped in `{ result }`: read `structuredContent`, not `structuredContent.result`. (#3081)
- **The bundled Ajv validator uses fast-uri 3.1.8.** It rejects a `$id` or `$ref` with an invalid URI scheme, such as `my_tool:output`. (#3083)

## New

- **Skills over MCP (SEP-2640).** A server publishes a folder of skills with `loadSkills(folder)` and `skills.attach(server)`; a client lists, reads and verifies them with `SkillsClient`. It works on 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. `attach` is experimental and may change in a minor release. (#3047, #3080)
- **Opt-in `scope` on token refresh.** Implement `scopeForRefresh(tokens)` on your `OAuthClientProvider` for an authorization server that rejects a refresh without `scope` (Microsoft Entra ID, `AADSTS90009`). The default request does not change. (#3085)
- `ServerEvent` takes optional `params`, so a gateway can forward change notifications with their `_meta`. (#3057)
- The v1 to v2 upgrade guide is also an installable agent skill. (#2968)

## Fixes

- `update({ title })` on a resource or resource template shows up in list responses. (#3005)
- A `Server` connected to a per-request transport at a modern revision binds that revision instead of answering `-32022`. (#3057)
- `createMcpHandler` sends `Allow: POST` on every `405`. (#3002)
- `@modelcontextprotocol/node` accepts `@hono/node-server` 1.x or 2.x; a new install resolves 2.x. (#3084)

items.name: @modelcontextprotocol/server@2.4.0
items.body:
### Minor Changes

- [#3057](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3057) [`c05225a`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/c05225a636c679870b65f8ca4fe83a76ea1cf113) Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete)! - `ServerEvent` takes optional `params`, which the `subscriptions/listen` router delivers with its own subscription ID, so a gateway can forward change notifications with their `_meta` and extension params.

- [#3047](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3047) [`46d9c99`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/46d9c9921b6542e813c1ecc5f9fc964085e8e3bb) Thanks [@KKonstantinov](https://github.com/KKonstantinov), [@tobi-oye](https://github.com/tobi-oye), [@mattzcarey](https://github.com/mattzcarey)! - Add the Skills extension (SEP-2640), reachable through new `ext/skills` subpaths; package root exports are unchanged.
    - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills`: `SkillsExtension` (`attach(server)` serves `skills/list`, `skills/get`, `resources/directory/read` and a `skill://{+path}` resource template), `SkillsExtension.load(files)` returning a `SkillCatalog` with `entries` and `reload()`, the `SkillFiles` storage adapter with `memorySkillFiles`, `SkillSource` for generated catalogs, `skillEntry`, and `SkillCatalogError`. Invalid skills are skipped with a warning (`onWarning`), or fail under `strict`. A file whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is served as `text`, whatever its MIME type; any other file as a base64 `blob`.
    - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills/node`: `loadSkills(folder)` and `nodeSkillFiles(folder)`.
    - `@modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills`: `SkillsClient` with `list()` (throws on an invalid entry; `skipInvalid: true` keeps the valid ones and returns the rest in `invalid`), `get()`, `read(skill, path?)` (size, digest and `SKILL.md` frontmatter verified, `SkillVerificationError` on a mismatch; a copy from the response cache that fails a check is fetched once more with `cacheMode: 'refresh'` first) and `readDirectory()`.
    - `@modelcontextprotocol/core/ext/skills`: schemas, types and constants, including `SKILL_LIMITS`. The result schemas follow the stable spec, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are required.

    `SkillsExtension.attach` is `@experimental`: how an extension is wired to a server may change in a minor release. The rest of the Skills API is stable.

    Works on 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. On 2026-07-28 only, the server sends the caching fields (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope`), and `SkillsClient` requires them and returns them from `list()`, `get()` and `readDirectory()`.

### Patch Changes

- [#3083](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3083) [`ef38c67`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/ef38c6765a15ee29030340dfea28b013893fa0a2) Thanks [@claude](https://github.com/apps/claude)! - The bundled Ajv validator is now built with fast-uri 3.1.8 (was 3.1.0). fast-uri 3.1.6 and later reject a `$id` or `$ref` whose text before the first colon is not a valid URI scheme (`my_tool:output`), or whose URN namespace is not valid (`urn:my_tool:output`): a schema that uses one no longer compiles, and a tool that carries it fails with an invalid-schema error. An underscore without a colon (`my_tool_output`) and a `$ref` into `#/$defs/...` or `#/definitions/...` are not affected.

- [#2960](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2960) [`43c45f4`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/43c45f4941d824e7251a7d1266823a84af90fab3) Thanks [@claude](https://github.com/apps/claude)! - A server whose tool puts `x-mcp-header` on a `number`-typed parameter keeps checking that tool's `Mcp-Param-*` headers on `tools/call`, as 2.3.0 does: a header that is missing for a value in the body, or that disagrees with the body, is answered `400` with JSON-RPC error `-32020`. Clients on a 2026-07-28 connection other than stdio no longer list such a tool and send no `Mcp-Param-*` headers for it, so a call that carries a value for a declared parameter is rejected the same way; the server logs a warning each time tools are listed. Use an integer (`z.int()`) or remove the annotation.

- [#3081](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3081) [`5820f79`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/5820f796a48ae6b8e756a7fbfd627e7e2e1ac891) Thanks [@claude](https://github.com/apps/claude)! - A tool `outputSchema` whose root is a `$ref` to a `type: "object"` entry of its own `$defs` or `definitions` (what zod writes for `z.object({...}).meta({ id })`), or a union of such refs, is now treated as an object schema. On 2025-era connections the tool's schema and `structuredContent` are no longer wrapped in `{ result: ... }`, so a 2025-era client that read `structuredContent.result` for such a tool now reads `structuredContent`. On every era the advertised schema gains `type: "object"` at its root.

- [#3057](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3057) [`c05225a`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/c05225a636c679870b65f8ca4fe83a76ea1cf113) Thanks [@steipete](https://github.com/steipete)! - Connecting a `Server` or `McpServer` to a `PerRequestHTTPServerTransport` classified at a modern revision that `supportedProtocolVersions` lists and the SDK implements now binds that revision, instead of answering `-32022`.

- [#3005](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3005) [`b381559`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/b381559edc0dbe25ab8324cada345b49bd1d2fc4) Thanks [@chaeyn](https://github.com/chaeyn)! - Reflect resource and resource template `update({ title })` changes in list responses. Preserve other metadata and individual resource titles when a template supplies list entries.

- [#3002](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3002) [`895007f`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/895007fe728b9c57fbe3ed45fe279ddc51f731f7) Thanks [@Hugo-DDT](https://github.com/Hugo-DDT)! - `createMcpHandler` now sends `Allow: POST` on every `405` it answers to a non-POST request, with `legacy: 'stateless'` (the default) and with `legacy: 'reject'`.

- [#2762](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2762) [`b022522`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/b022522089a0c8b632595c6e7b536453945ed5a9) Thanks [@pcarleton](https://github.com/pcarleton)! - `x-mcp-header` on a `number`-typed tool parameter is now rejected, matching the 2026-07-28 spec ("Parameters with type `number` are not permitted"; clients MUST exclude such tools from `tools/list`). Previously `number` was accepted only to satisfy an older conformance fixture that has since been corrected. `integer`, `string` and `boolean` are unaffected.

- Updated dependencies [[`46d9c99`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/46d9c9921b6542e813c1ecc5f9fc964085e8e3bb)]:
    - @modelcontextprotocol/core@2.4.0

Invalid skills are skipped with a warning (`onWarning`), or fail under `strict`. A file whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is served as `text`, whatever its MIME type; any other file as a base64 `blob`.
    - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills/node`: `loadSkills(folder)` and `nodeSkillFiles(folder)`.
    - `@modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills`: `SkillsClient` with `list()` (throws on an invalid entry; `skipInvalid: true` keeps the valid ones and returns the rest in `invalid`), `get()`, `read(skill, path?)` (size, digest and `SKILL.md` frontmatter verified, `SkillVerificationError` on a mismatch; a copy from the response cache that fails a check is fetched once more with `cacheMode: 'refresh'` first) and `readDirectory()`.
    - `@modelcontextprotocol/core/ext/skills`: schemas, types and constants, including `SKILL_LIMITS`. The result schemas follow the stable spec, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are required.

    `SkillsExtension.attach` is `@experimental`: how an extension is wired to a server may change in a minor release. The rest of the Skills API is stable.

    Works on 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. On 2026-07-28 only, the server sends the caching fields (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope`), and `SkillsClient` requires them and returns them from `list()`, `get()` and `readDirectory()`.

## What's Changed
* fix: add explicit | undefined to Transport optional properties (v1.x backport of #1766) by @kishormorol in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2814
* [v1.x] fix: allow registering after connect() when the capability was declared by @claude[bot] in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2958
* chore: bump version to 1.32.2 by @claude[bot] in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3089

## New Contributors
* @kishormorol made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2814

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/compare/1.32.1...1.32.2

items.name: v0.40.9
items.body:
## Flint on Linux and Windows

[Flint](https://ollama.com/library/flint) now runs on Linux and Windows as well as macOS.

## Other improvements

- Streaming OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages requests now report generation failures instead of ending silently after partial output.
- `ollama launch` now passes cloud models' context lengths and capabilities to coding tools, fixing incorrect context and compaction settings.
- Anthropic-compatible web search now uses the model's supported thinking setting in follow-up requests, preventing avoidable failures.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.8...v0.40.9

items.name: v0.40.8
items.body: ## Recursive Flint [Flint](https://ollama.com/library/flint) brings Recursive's coding model to Ollama. It is designed for the work coding agents do across a repository: understanding unfamiliar code, tracing bugs, implementing features, and adding tests. Reasoning, multi-turn tool use, and a 262K-token context window support longer tasks across files and tool interactions. Flint is an Apache 2.0-licensed, 40B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with approximately 2.5B parameters active per token. In its [release evaluations](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint#evaluation), Recursive reports 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified. ```sh ollama run flint ``` Note: Flint is supported on MacOS. Other GPU support will be enabled in a subsequent release. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.7...v0.40.8
